This is a standard **Support Escalation Policy** template. It is designed to be modular, so you can adapt the specific roles (e.g., changing "Engineer" to "Developer") to fit your specific organizational structure. --- # Support Escalation Policy ## 1. Purpose The purpose of this policy is to ensure that customer inquiries and technical issues are resolved efficiently by directing them to the appropriate level of expertise. This policy aims to minimize resolution time (MTTR), prevent "ticket bouncing" between agents, and ensure that high-level engineering resources are used only when necessary. ## 2. Scope This policy applies to all customer-facing support staff, technical account managers, and engineering teams involved in the product lifecycle. ## 3. Support Tier Definitions ### Tier 1: Frontline Support (Generalists) * **Role:** Customer Success Associates / Support Agents. * **Focus:** High-volume, low-complexity inquiries. * **Responsibilities:** * Initial triage and ticket categorization. * Answering "How-to" questions using the Knowledge Base (KB). * Basic troubleshooting (password resets, account provisioning, UI navigation). * Gathering essential information (account IDs, screenshots, steps to reproduce). * Managing customer expectations and communication. ### Tier 2: Technical Support (Specialists) * **Role:** Senior Support Engineers / Technical Support Specialists. * **Focus:** Medium-to-high complexity technical issues. * **Responsibilities:** * Deep-dive troubleshooting of configuration and integration issues. * Analyzing system logs and error reports. * Investigating database entries or API responses. * Managing complex account setups or data migrations. * Identifying potential software bugs to be reported to Tier 3. ### Tier 3: Engineering/Product Support (Subject Matter Experts) * **Role:** Software Engineers / DevOps / Product Managers. * **Focus:** High-complexity, code-level, or infrastructure-level issues. * **Responsibilities:** * Resolving confirmed software bugs and code defects. * Addressing server-side, database, or architectural failures. * Implementing hotfixes or security patches. * Developing new features or workarounds for systemic product limitations. --- ## 4. Escalation Triggers (The "When") To maintain efficiency, staff must follow these triggers to move a ticket between tiers. | From $\rightarrow$ To | Trigger Criteria (When to Escalate) | Required Documentation | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Tier 1 $\rightarrow$ Tier 2** | • Issue cannot be resolved using existing Knowledge Base articles.
• Issue requires administrative permissions Tier 1 does not possess.
• Issue involves complex integrations or API errors.
• The customer is a "High Value/Enterprise" account requiring specialized handling. | • Summary of steps already attempted.
• Customer environment details (OS, Browser, Version).
• Error messages/screenshots. | | **Tier 2 $\rightarrow$ Tier 3** | • The issue is identified as a confirmed software bug (not user error).
• The issue requires a change to the source code or database schema.
• The issue involves a system-wide outage or critical security vulnerability.
• Troubleshooting has exhausted all Tier 2 diagnostic tools. | • **Full Reproduction Steps:** A guaranteed way to trigger the error.
• **Logs:** Relevant server/API logs.
• **Impact Statement:** Number of users affected and severity. | --- ## 5. Escalation Protocol (The "How") ### 5.1 Internal Communication When escalating, the agent must not simply "transfer" the ticket. They must "hand over" the ticket. A successful escalation must include: 1. **The "What":** A clear, concise description of the problem. 2. **The "Tried":** A detailed list of every troubleshooting step already performed (to prevent Tier 2/3 from repeating Tier 1's work). 3. **The "Evidence":** Logs, screenshots, or video recordings. ### 5.2 Customer Communication * **Transparency:** When a ticket is escalated, the customer must be notified: *"I am escalating this to our Senior Engineering team to investigate the root cause. I will provide an update by [Time/Date]."* * **Ownership:** The original agent remains the "Owner" of the customer relationship, even if a Tier 3 engineer is working on the technical fix. The agent should act as the bridge to ensure the customer is not left in the dark. ## 6. Policy Review This policy shall be reviewed quarterly by the Support Manager and Head of Engineering to adjust tier boundaries based on product complexity and team performance metrics.
